fatigue, and significant weight loss, subsequently found to have 
multiple lesions of the spine, skull, and brain concerning for 
metastatic malignancy.

# Metastatic malignancy, unknown primary: On this admission, 
patient presented with significant radicular back pain in the 
setting of weight loss and continued fatigue. Patient was assess 
for his back pain with imaging, which was notable for metastatic 
disease burden, with multiple soft tissue and bony lesions 
involving the spine, liver, brain, lung and multiple bone 
locations identified. Patient underwent an uncomplicated Right 
pelvic biopsy on ___, and tissue was sent for pathological 
analysis. Initial pathology was notable for malignant cells, 
likely adenocarcinoma. Final pathology was notable for carcinoma 
strongly positive for CK7, positive for CDX2, and negative for 
CK20, PAX8, and TTF-1, which although not specific, was 
suggestive of a pancreaticobiliary,  upper GI or colorectal 
origin. An EGD was performed on this admission which was was 
unremarkable for a notable GI mass. PET CT was notable for 
extensive FDG avid metastatic disease throughout the bilateral 
lungs, mediastinum, right hilum, liver, left gluteal 
musculature, and osseous structures, with nodefinitive primary 
malignancy identified by PET. However, based on patients 
distribution of disease with significant pulmonary disease 
burden including a 4.2cm right suprahilar mass obstructing the 
SVC and innumerable pulmonary metastases in all lobes (larges in 
RLL up to 1.9cm) and relatively little GI involvement (hepatic 
lesions were noted to be like harmatomas rather than metastatic 
disease), concern remained high for a primary lung cancer with 
lung adenocarcinoma being a likely candidate to explain patients 
presentation and metastatic disease burden. Due to patients 
multiple spinal mets, patient was assessed by ortho spine who 
noted patient could remain weight bearing as tolerated. Due to 
patients extensive brain metastases, patient was assessed by 
radiation oncology, and plan was made for patient to receive 
WBRT. Patient received 5 treatments of WBRT, which he tolerated 
well. Patients R thigh was also treated with 5 doses of XRT 
external beam radiation as this was a focus of significant pain 
for patient and had bony met involvement. Following treatment 
with WBRT, patient required XRT to spine from T1 to T8 due to 
progressive metastatic disease with concern for cord impingement 
(see below). Despite being a TTF-1 negative staining indicating 
a non-lung process, plan was made to approach patients cancer as 
adenocarcinoma of unknown primary vs non-small cell lung 
carcinoma, with plan for followup in thoracic oncology  
following acute rehab to improve strength and mobility.

narrowing or cord impingement. Due to notable mets with concern

narrowing, patient was planned for 5 doses of XRT to the T1 to

improvement in his back pain. Patient completed his 5 planned

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Multiple pulmonary nodules are re-demonstrated in the lung bases.
Small right pleural effusion from previous film has resolved.  Mild
subsegmental atelectasis seen at right lung base.  No pericardial effusion
seen.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: There are multiple hypodense lesions within the liver, overall
still too small to characterize, but likely representing biliary hamartomas
versus less likely metastases or cysts.  The largest hypodense lesion seen we

evidence of focal lesions.

consistent with recent PET-CT.

URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram.
There is a 1.3 cm cyst that is reidentified in the right mid to lower kidney. 
There are no focal lesions of the left kidney.  .  There is no perinephric
abnormality.  No hydronephrosis is appreciated bilaterally.

normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The colon and
rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized.

thoracolumbar spine and pelvis.  Permeative lesion in L4 vertebral body with

right acetabulum is demonstrated with associated soft tissue component which

1. No hydronephrosis.

from ___.

INDICATION:  History of metastatic cancer, likely lung adenocarcinoma with new
finding of T1 vertebral body lesion with possible erosion into the spinal
canal.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal imaging was performed with T2, T1, and STIR technique. 
Axial T2 imaging was performed. Axial GRE images of the cervical spine were

FINDINGS: 

THORACIC:
Again, there are numerous T1 hypointense T2 hyperintense enhancing lesions
throughout the thoracic spine compatible with diffuse osseous metastatic
disease, as seen on the recent prior MR examination from ___.  There
is diffuse involvement of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the right
pedicle and facet with extra cortical extension into the epidural space at the
level the right pedicle by about 3 mm (18:3).  Another area of involvement is
within the T8 vertebral body where a rounded lesion in the vertebral body
measuring 17 mm has increased in size, previously 15 mm and there is extension
and expansion of the right pedicle and facet, now with further expansion and
with involvement of the spinous process.  There is extra cortical extension
into the epidural space, shifting the cord the left causing mild canal
stenosis at this level without impingement.  There is extension of roughly 6
mm into the epidural space (19:36).  Involvement from T9 through T12 has also
progressed compared to the prior examination, in particular the superior left
aspect of the T12 vertebral body where a smaller lesions have now coalesced
into a larger lesion measuring at least 33 x 15 mm.  Vertebral body heights
are otherwise maintained without evidence of pathologic fracture degenerative
changes appear similar to the ___ examination.  Spinal cord signal
and morphology is normal.

LUMBAR:  Again seen are areas of marrow placement with the post gadolinium
enhancement in the L1, L4, L5 and S3 vertebral bodies.  At L1, multiple
lesions are seen coalescing at the left aspect of the superior vertebral body
which appears increased compared to the prior examination, for example at the
anterior superior endplate 18 x 16 mm lesion previously measured 14 x 12 mm. 
Again, there is extension into the left pedicle and facet and another rounded
lesion is seen at the spinous process at this level measuring 12 x 10 mm,
previously 6 x 6 mm (12:11).  Again, there is diffuse involvement of the L4
vertebral body with extension to the bilateral pedicles which appears
progressed, with further extension of the right pedicle with probable trace
soft tissue extension into the anterior epidural space.  There is also
prevertebral soft tissue enhancement appearing similar to the prior
examination likely representing cortical breakthrough.  8 mm lesion in the
posterior aspect of the L3 vertebral body is new.  There is also involvement
of the left L5 pedicle and facet as well as the posterior superior endplate
which appears mildly progressed compared the prior examination.

Scattered degenerative changes appears similar to the prior examination. 
Again seen is a fracture line parallel to the superior endplate of the L4
vertebral body with minimal superior endplate compression though the remainder
of the vertebral body height is relatively well maintained.  Spinal cord
signal and morphology is normal.

OTHER: There is a 1.2 cm right interpolar renal cyst.  Mild right
hydroureteronephrosis is new and is not fully characterize.  Several punctate
T2 hyperintense liver lesions are partially visualized.  Several enhancing
lung lesions are partially visualized, measuring up to 1.9 cm with spiculation
in the right lung base.

IMPRESSION:


1. Progressive osseous metastatic disease, as described in detail above. 
There is extra cortical soft tissue extension at T1, T8 and L4 vertebral
bodies with encroachment to the epidural space without resultant high-grade
spinal canal narrowing or cord impingement.
2. Normal cord signal.
3. Unchanged mild pathologic superior endplate compression fracture of the L4
vertebral body.
4. New mild right hydroureteronephrosis, incompletely characterized.
5. Numerous pulmonary lesions partially visualized, corresponding to known
metastases.
6. Innumerable T2 hyperintense hepatic lesions are incompletely characterized.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Consider CT urogram for further evaluation of new right
hydroureteronephrosis.

PROCEDURE

thrombectomy system and cleaner
4. Right brachiocephalic and subclavian angioplasty with 10 mm balloon

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the explanation of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The right arm, right groin, and left groin were prepped and draped
in the usual sterile fashion.

Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right basilic vein was
compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle.  Permanent images were
obtained before and after intravenous access, which confirmed a vein patency. 
An 0.018 wire was passed into the axillary vein.  The micropuncture sheath was
advanced over the wire.  A right upper extremity venogram was performed.  A
___ wire was advanced through the sheath.  A 5 ___ sheath was advanced
over the wire.  An MPA catheter and Glidewire were used to try and cross the
SVC occlusion.  These attempts were not successful.  Attention was turned
towards the right groin.

Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right common femoral vein was
compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent images were
obtained before and after intravenous access, which confirmed a vein patency. 
A ___ wire was advanced into the IVC.  An 8 ___ 45 cm bright tip sheath
was advanced over the wire into the IVC.  An MPA catheter and Glidewire were
used to cross the SVC stenosis.  Mechanical thrombectomy was performed using
Penumbra Cat 8 suction thrombectomy catheter and a Cleaner device. 
Angioplasty of the right brachiocephalic and subclavian vein was performed
using a 10 mm balloon.   2 mg of tPA was infused through a catheter into the
clot.  Multiple rounds of thrombectomy were repeated.

Doctors ___ and ___ now joined the procedure.  Dr. ___ the
left CFV port placement.

Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent left common femoral vein was
compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent ultrasound
images were obtained before and after intravenous access, which confirmed vein
patency. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the IVC using
fluoroscopic guidance. The needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath.
The Nitinol wire was removed and a short ___ wire was advanced to make
appropriate measurements for catheter length. The ___ wire was then passed
distally into the IVC.
Next, attention was turned towards creation of a subcutaneous pocket over the
left lateral thigh.  A 2.5 cm transverse incision was made and a subcutaneous
pocket was created by using blunt dissection. The single lumen port was then
connected to the catheter.  The catheter was tunneled from the subcutaneous
pocket towards the venotomy site from where it was brought out using a
tunneling device. The port was then connected to the catheter and checks were
made for any leakage by accessing the diaphragm using a non-coring ___
needle. No leaks were found.
The port was then placed in the subcutaneous pocket and secured with ___
ethilon sutures on either side. The venotomy tract was dilated using the
introducer of the peel-away sheath supplied. Following this, the peel-away
sheath was placed over the ___ wire through which the port was threaded into
the right side of the heart with the tip in the right atrium.  The sheath was
then peeled away.
The subcutaneous pocket was closed with ___ subcuticular continuous Vicryl
sutures.  ___ subcuticular Vicryl sutures and Steri-strips were used to close
the venotomy incision site. Steri-Strips were applied over the sutures.

At this time, blood could not be aspirated from the port.  Contrast injection
confirmed that the port tip was again see right atrium wall.  Sutures were cut
and the catheter was shortened.  The catheter course at the venotomy site was
also massaged to reduced kinks.  The port pocket was again closed in the same
fashion.  Final spot fluoroscopic image demonstrating good alignment of the
catheter and no kinking. The tip is in the right atrium.  The port was
accessed using a non coring ___ needle and could be aspirated and flushed
easily. Sterile dressings were applied.  The port was left accessed as
requested.

3500 units of intravenous heparin was now administered.  Repeat angioplasty of
the right subclavian and brachiocephalic veins was performed with a 10 mm
balloon.  12 mm balloon angioplasty of the SVC was performed.  Right upper
extremity venogram demonstrated central patency of the right brachiocephalic
and subclavian veins.  Multiple planning venograms were performed.  A 14 mm x
6 cm Luminexx stent was deployed from the right brachiocephalic SVC junction
to the lower SVC.  The stent was dilated with a 12 mm balloon.  1500 units of
intravenous heparin was administered.  Additional angioplasty of the right
brachiocephalic vein was performed with the 10 mm balloon.  Final right upper
extremity venograms were performed.

Patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate postprocedural
complications.  The patient was extubated and transferred to the PACU in good
condition.

thrombectomy and angioplasty.
5. High-grade SVC stenosis substantially improved after angioplasty and
stenting.

1. Successful thrombectomy and recannulization of a completely thrombosed
right brachiocephalic and subclavian vein
2. Successful SVC stenting
